messages.content: What is the Manacher algorithm for palindrome
Find longest palindromic substring in O(n) linear time using mirror properties and center expansion.
Explain the suffix array construction
Build sorted array of all suffixes in O(n log^2 n) or O(n) with advanced techniques.
What is the longest palindromic subsequence
DP variant of LCS with reversed string; O(n^2) time and space.
Explain the substring palindrome queries
Precompute or use Manacher; enable O(1) queries after O(n) prep.
What is the minimum palindrome partitions
DP where dp[i] = min partitions for s[:i]. O(n^2) time.
Explain graph coloring and chromatic number
NP-hard; greedy: O(n+m) gives chi+1 colors. Exact via backtracking or DP.
What is the four color theorem
Every planar graph 4-colorable; proof by computer exhaustion.
Explain interval scheduling maximization
Greedy: sort by end time, pick earliest-ending intervals. O(n log n).
What is the weighted interval scheduling
DP: sort by end time, find latest non-overlapping for each interval.
Explain the activity selection problem
Same as interval scheduling; greedy optimal due to greedy choice property.
What is the independent set problem
Max set of non-adjacent vertices; NP-hard; tree/bipartite: polynomial.
Explain clique problem complexity
Find largest complete subgraph; NP-hard; no known poly approximation.
What is the vertex cover approximation
2-approximation: take endpoints of maximal matching.
Explain the 3-coloring problem
NP-complete; backtracking with heuristics in practice.
What is the dominating set problem
Min set such all vertices in set or adjacent; NP-hard; ln n approximation.
Explain the longest path in DAG
Topological sort then DP; linear time; NP-hard in general graphs.
What is the shortest path in DAG
Topological sort then DP; linear time; more efficient than Dijkstra.
Explain Hamiltonian path complexity
NP-complete; no known polynomial algorithm; exponential solutions.
What is the Eulerian path
Path using each edge once; greedy if degree constraint met; O(V+E).
Explain directed acyclic graph topological sort
Linear time via DFS; enables DP on DAGs.
What is the maximum independent set tree
Greedily take non-adjacent; DP on tree: dp[v][0/1] for include/exclude.
Explain tree diameter
Two-pass BFS/DFS; first to find far point, second from that point.
What is the tree radius
Minimum eccentricity; O(n) once diameter is known.
Explain tree centroid
Node with min max subtree size; useful for divide-and-conquer decomposition.
What is the all pairs shortest path
Floyd-Warshall: O(n^3). Or Dijkstra from each: O(n(m+n)log n).
Explain transitive closure
Reachability between all pairs; Floyd-Warshall with OR instead of min.
What is the strongly connected components
Kosaraju or Tarjan; O(V+E); components form DAG structure.
Explain bridge and articulation
Tarjan-style DFS finds cut edges and vertices in O(V+E).
What is the 2-edge connected components
Contract bridges; components remain connected after any single edge removal.
Explain tree rerooting DP
Recompute DP for each root; O(n) after initial O(n) root choice.
What is the small to large merging
DSU optimization: merge smaller into larger for O(n log^2 n).
Explain Knuth optimization in DP
Monotonicity of optimal split point; reduces O(n^3) to O(n^2).
What is the convex hull trick
Geometry optimization; maintain lower envelope of lines for DP queries.
Explain slope optimization
Slope trick in DP; abs function optimization via line parametrization.
What is the matrix chain order
Catalan number of ways; DP with optimal split point monge property.
Explain the egg drop problem
k eggs, n floors; DP with binary search reduces to O(n log n).
What is the coin change variations
Count ways, min coins, max coins; different DP formulations.
Explain the longest increasing subarray
Greedy; reset on decrease; O(n) time.
What is the maximum subarray sum variants
Kadane for 1D; 2D via prefix sums; max k subarrays uses DP.
Explain shortest superstring
TSP on strings with overlaps; NP-hard; 2-approximation via MST.
What is the subset sum problem variants
0/1: NP-hard; unbounded: DP; bounded: pseudo-polynomial.
Explain the 0/1 knapsack optimizations
Space: O(W) using 1D DP. Time: no better than O(nW) known.
What is the approximation algorithm PTAS
Polynomial time approximation scheme; O(n^{1/eps}) runtime.
Explain the greedy algorithm analysis
Prove optimal via exchange argument or activity selection structure.
What is the randomized quicksort
O(n log n) expected; O(n^2) worst case; in-place.
Explain the randomized selection
Quickselect: O(n) expected, O(n^2) worst; linear via median-of-medians.
What is the skip list vs balanced tree
Skip list simpler, similar bounds; no rotation needed.
Explain the randomized incremental construction
Build incrementally adding random points; analyze in reverse.
What is the derandomization technique
Convert randomized to deterministic; expands algorithm complexity.
Explain the Las Vegas vs Monte Carlo
Las Vegas: always correct, random time. Monte Carlo: random correctness.
What is the probabilistic method
Prove existence via probability; often non-constructive.
Explain the Lovasz local lemma
Dependencies allow constructive proof despite bad events.
What is the union bound and Chernoff
Bound on probability of bad events; Chernoff tighter for binomial.
Explain the Markov inequality bound
E[X] >= k*P(X >= k); loose but distribution-free.
What is the autocorrelation polynomial
FFT convolution enables fast substring matching and longest palindrome.
Explain the string periodicity
Detect repetitions; related to failure function in KMP.
What is the Lyndon word factorization
Decompose string into decreasing Lyndon words; applications in sorting.
Explain the weak periodicity
Fractional periods; harder to detect than full periods.
What is the palindrome factorization
Decompose into palindromes; minimum partitions in polynomial time.
Explain the reverse string processing
Suffix arrays, suffix trees enable pattern matching, longest palindrome.
What is the binary string matching
Pattern matching on bits; rolling hash with modular arithmetic.
Explain the dictionary compression
Lempel-Ziv, Huffman; variable-length encoding for text.
What is the Burrows-Wheeler transform
Sortable rotation; used in bzip2; enables better compression.
Explain the rank and select
Succinct data structure support for bit operations in O(1) space.
What is the wavelet tree structure
Solves range queries in O(log sigma) where sigma is alphabet.
Explain the cartesian tree
Recursively for min/max; enables RMQ in O(1) after O(n) prep.
What is the sparse table
2^k preprocessing for RMQ; O(1) query after O(n log n) prep.
Explain the monotonic deque optimization
Maintain deque of useful elements for sliding window min/max.
What is the monotonic stack usage
Find next greater element; enables O(n) for span, histogram problems.
Explain the segment tree lazy propagation
Range updates O(log n); pushes down only when accessed.
What is the persistent segment tree
All versions accessible; enables point-in-time queries.
Explain the implicit segment tree
Compress coordinate space; solves problems on infinite range.
What is the dynamic segment tree
Node generation on demand; handles sparse updates efficiently.
Explain the Fenwick tree range updates
Difference array technique enables O(log n) range assignment.
What is the 2D Fenwick tree
2D prefix sums; O(log^2 n) per operation.
Explain the merge sort tree
Sorted sequence at each node; enables O(log^2 n) range queries.
What is the palindrome tree
Explicit representation of all palindromic substrings; O(n) construction.
Explain the AC automaton complexities
Build: O(sum of lengths); search: O(n); reports in O(n+z).
What is the XOR basis linear algebra
Basis of vectors under XOR; solves max XOR pair.
Explain the Gaussian elimination XOR
Apply to solve XOR system of equations in O(n^3).
What is the matroid intersection
Common base in two matroids via augmenting paths.
Explain the bipartite matching hopcroft
O(E sqrt(V)) via blocking flows; practical best algorithm.
What is the push-relabel flow
Preflow algorithm: O(V^3) or O(V^2 E) with heuristics.
Explain the dinic flow algorithm
O(V^2 E) via level graphs and blocking flows.
What is the minimum cost maximum flow
Successive shortest paths with potential; SPFA or Dijkstra.
Explain the project selection problem
Max flow reduction of selection with profits and dependencies.
What is the image segmentation graph cut
Min-cut gives optimal energy minimization in computer vision.
Explain the transportation problem
Bipartite with supplies/demands; min cost flow solution.
What is the assignment problem Hungarian
Optimal matching; reduces to min cost flow or uses auction algorithm.
Explain the maximum closure
Find largest closure with min cut; useful for project selection.
What is the minimum st-cut max flow
By max flow min cut theorem; solves many optimization problems.
Explain the Gomory-Hu tree building
n-1 max flows construct implicit min cut representation.
What is the submodular function
Diminishing returns property; enables efficient optimization.
Explain the matroid definition
Set of independent sets closed under exchange axioms.
What is the graphic matroid
Independent sets correspond to forests in graph.
Explain the linear matroid
Linearly independent vectors; basis matrix operations.
What is the greedy algorithm matroid
Greedily pick max weight; optimal for matroids.
Explain the matroid union
Union of matroids; allows more complex greedy problems.
What is the parametric search
Decide feasibility as function of parameter then binary search.
Explain the simulation of simplicity
Perturb coordinates infinitesimally to resolve degeneracies.
What is the sweepline algorithm convex hull
Sort by angle, maintain convex hull incrementally.
Explain the rotating calipers
Maintain antipodal pairs during hull rotation for all diameter pairs.
What is the halfplane intersection
Find feasible region of half-plane constraints via sweepline.
Explain the point location
Preprocess polygon for fast point membership queries.
What is the orthogonal range search
Query points in axis-aligned rectangle; 2D range trees O(log^2 n).
Explain the fractional cascading two
Cascade on secondary structures for O(log n + k) results.
What is the dynamic convex hull
Insert/delete points, maintain hull; O(log^2 n) per operation.
Explain the 3D convex hull
Incremental construction with O(n log n) time via halfspaces.
What is the Delaunay flip
Swap diagonal if improves max angle; terminates to Delaunay.
Explain the Voronoi dual
Delaunay edges dual to Voronoi edges; mutual relationships.
What is the medial axis
Skeleton of shape; center of maximal balls inside.
Explain the motion planning
Plan robot path avoiding obstacles; roadmap or cell decomposition.
What is the Minkowski sum
All sum vectors; useful for collision detection.
Explain the trapezoidal decomposition
Decompose polygon; enables O(log n) point location.
What is the plane sweep for visibility
Find visible region from point in O(n log n).
Explain the Triangulation ear clipping
Repeatedly remove ears of simple polygon in O(n^2).
What is the monotone polygon triangulation
Linear time via sweep and stack of monotone polygon.
Explain the 2D point processing
Applications of convex hull, Voronoi, Delaunay combined.
What is the planar graph duality
Dual graph has edges crossing original edges.
Explain the Euler characteristic
V - E + F = 2 for planar; enables spanning tree facts.
What is the planar separator theorem
O(sqrt(n)) vertex separator exists; divide and conquer.
Explain the planar tester Hopcroft-Tarjan
O(n) planarity testing via DFS and PQ-trees.
What is the outerplanar graph
Planar with single face; tree-like structure.
Explain the series parallel graph
Recursive construction; enable efficient algorithms.
What is the approximation hardness
NP-hard to approximate within certain factors.
Explain the inapproximability
Gap problems show hardness of approximation bounds.
What is the PCP theorem
Probabilistically checkable proofs; implies inapproximability.
Explain the approximation lower bounds
Hardness results via gap instances or reductions.
What is the randomized rounding
Round LP solution probabilistically; get approximate solution.
Explain the primal-dual method
Iteratively improve primal and dual for approximation.
What is the Lagrangian relaxation
Relax constraints into objective; iteratively improve.
Explain the subgradient method
Optimize non-smooth Lagrangian; used in integer programming.
What is the column generation
Dynamically add variables; useful for large LP instances.
Explain the cutting planes iterative
Add cuts; tighten relaxation polytope toward integer hull.
What is the Benders decomposition
Decompose into master and subproblems via dual.
Explain the Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition
Reformulate via convex combination of extreme points.
What is the local search metaheuristic
Iteratively improve solution in neighborhood; escape local minima.
Explain the tabu search
Forbid recent moves to avoid cycles in local search.
What is the simulated annealing
Accept worse solutions with decreasing temperature.
Explain the genetic algorithm
Population-based evolution via selection, crossover, mutation.
What is the particle swarm optimization
Swarm intelligence mimicking bird flocking behavior.
Explain the ant colony optimization
Pheromone-based construction used for TSP and routing.
What is the differential evolution
Population-based for continuous optimization.
Explain the cross-entropy method
Iteratively update distribution to maximize probability.
What is the noise injection
Add randomness to escape local optima in optimization.
Explain the neighborhood structure
Define which solutions are neighbors in local search.
What is the landscape analysis
Study optimization objective function structure.
Explain the fitness landscape
Visualize function values as terrain in high-dimensional space.
What is the no free lunch theorem
No algorithm optimal for all functions; problem-dependent.
Explain the oracle complexity
Lower bounds on number of function evaluations needed.
What is the query complexity lower bound
Adversary argument shows optimization needs many queries.
Explain the information theory lower bound
Entropy argument bounds on problem difficulty.
What is the communication complexity
Bits needed to solve problem with distributed algorithm.
Explain the VLSI layout
Physical design of circuits on chip; NP-hard optimization.
What is the register allocation
Assign variables to CPU registers minimizing spills.
Explain the instruction scheduling
Order instructions maximizing parallelism respecting dependencies.
What is the cache optimization
Reorder computation to improve cache locality.
Explain the branch prediction
Speculate on branch outcomes to avoid pipeline stall.
What is the software pipelining
Overlap iterations of loop via rescheduling instructions.
Explain the loop fusion optimization
Merge loops to improve cache behavior.
What is the loop tiling
Partition iteration space into tiles for cache reuse.
Explain the vectorization SIMD
Exploit vector instructions for parallel computation.
What is the GPU computation
Massively parallel execution on graphics processors.
Explain the MapReduce framework
Distributed processing of big data via map and reduce.
What is the Spark RDD
Resilient distributed datasets enabling iterative algorithms.
Explain the stream processing
Process continuous data streams with bounded memory.
What is the online algorithm
Decides on input elements without future knowledge.
Explain the competitive ratio
Online solution vs offline optimum bound in worst case.
What is the adversarial input model
Adversary constructs worst-case input for online algorithm.
Explain the list scheduling problem
Online scheduling without knowing future jobs.
What is the paging replacement
Online cache replacement; LRU is optimal offline vs 2*OPT.
Explain the load balancing online
Assign jobs to machines without knowing future.
What is the two-server problem
Move two servers to cover requests; open problem.
Explain the k-server conjecture
k-server competitive ratio equals k; proven for k <= 2.
Explain the secretary problem analysis
Optimal threshold: reject first n/e candidates, pick first exceeding threshold.
What is the online bipartite matching
Greedy or randomized algorithm; 1/2-competitive for general graph.
Explain the online shortest path
Traverse graph discovering edges; expansion ratio is competitive measure.
What is the TCP congestion control
Online algorithm adjusting window size based on packet loss.
Explain the online routing protocol
Route packets without global network knowledge.
What is the machine learning regret
Bound difference from optimal; relates to online algorithm competitive ratio.
Explain the bandit algorithm
Explore-exploit tradeoff; Thompson sampling, UCB strategies.
What is the multi-armed bandit
Sequential decision maximizing cumulative reward.
Explain the contextual bandit extension
Use context information to inform arm selection.
What is the reinforcement learning MDP
Markov decision process; optimal policy via Bellman equations.
Explain the value iteration algorithm
Fixed point iteration computing optimal values from Bellman.
What is the policy iteration algorithm
Alternate policy evaluation and improvement until convergence.
Explain the Q-learning algorithm
Off-policy learning updating action values from experience.
What is the temporal difference learning
Update value using bootstrap from subsequent state.
Explain the actor-critic algorithm
Policy gradient method with value baseline.
What is the trust region policy
Constrain policy update within trust region for stability.
Explain the gradient descent convergence
Learning rate determines convergence speed and final accuracy.
What is the stochastic gradient descent
Mini-batch updates provide noisy gradient estimates.
Explain the momentum acceleration
Accumulate gradient direction for faster convergence.
What is the Adam optimizer
Adaptive moments; per-parameter learning rates via exponential moving average.
Explain the RMSprop adaptation
Root mean square of gradients; normalizes step size per dimension.
What is the batch normalization
Normalize layer inputs for stability and faster training.
Explain the dropout regularization
Randomly disable neurons; ensemble effect reduces overfitting.
What is the L1/L2 regularization
Penalty on weights; L1 induces sparsity, L2 smoothness.
Explain the weight decay
L2 regularization in optimization; dampens parameter growth.
What is the cross-entropy loss
KL divergence between predicted and true distribution.
Explain the softmax function
Normalize logits to probability distribution.
What is the ReLU activation
Max(0, x); simple but effective; avoids vanishing gradient.
Explain the sigmoid activation
S-shaped; squashes to [0,1]; used for binary classification.
What is the tanh activation
Squashes to [-1,1]; zero-centered; better than sigmoid.
Explain the backpropagation algorithm
Compute gradients via chain rule in reverse topological order.
What is the vanishing gradient problem
Gradients shrink with depth; ReLU and skip connections help.
Explain the exploding gradient
Gradients grow large; gradient clipping prevents divergence.
What is the neural network approximation
Universal approximator with hidden layer; depth enables efficiency.
Explain the convolutional neural network
Local connectivity and weight sharing; efficient for images.
What is the recurrent neural network
Temporal dependencies via feedback connections; stateful.
Explain the LSTM cell
Gating mechanism controls information flow; addresses vanishing gradient.
What is the GRU simplified
Fewer gates than LSTM; often performs similarly.
Explain the bidirectional RNN
Process sequence forward and backward; aggregate both representations.
What is the attention mechanism
Query key value; compute weights over values based on query.
Explain the transformer architecture
Multi-head self-attention and feedforward; parallel processing.
What is the positional encoding
Encode position information into embeddings; enables ordering.
Explain the beam search decoding
Keep top-k hypotheses expanding each; find best sequence.
What is the greedy decoding
Pick most likely token at each step; fast but suboptimal.
Explain the sampling temperature
Scale logits before sampling; control randomness.
What is the top-k top-p sampling
Restrict sampling to most likely tokens; nucleus sampling.
Explain the maximum likelihood objective
Maximize probability of correct sequence; standard training.
What is the teacher forcing
Feed true tokens during training; distribution mismatch at test.
Explain the scheduled sampling
Gradually increase exposure to model outputs during training.
What is the copy mechanism
Attention to source enables copying relevant information.
Explain the pointer network
Attention instead of softmax over vocabulary; points to inputs.
What is the coverage mechanism
Track which inputs have been attended; prevent repetition.
Explain the multi-task learning
Train single model on multiple related tasks; shared representation.
What is the transfer learning
Train on source task, finetune on target; reduce data needs.
Explain the domain adaptation
Reduce distribution shift between source and target domains.
What is the meta-learning
Learn to learn; quick adaptation to new tasks.
Explain the few-shot learning
Adapt to new task from few examples; meta-learning application.
What is the zero-shot learning
Generalize to unseen classes; use semantic attributes.
Explain the continual learning
Learn new tasks without forgetting old ones.
What is the catastrophic forgetting
New learning overwrites old knowledge; memory replay helps.
Explain the knowledge distillation
Train student to mimic teacher; compress model.
What is the model compression pruning
Remove unimportant connections; maintain performance.
Explain the quantization low precision
Reduce bit width of weights and activations.
What is the neural architecture search
Automatically design network architecture; computationally expensive.
Explain the hyperparameter tuning
Grid or random search or Bayesian optimization over parameters.
What is the early stopping criteria
Monitor validation; stop when performance plateaus.
Explain the cross-validation strategy
k-fold provides multiple train-test splits for robust evaluation.
What is the class imbalance handling
Weighted loss, resampling, or SMOTE for minority class.
Explain the data augmentation
Artificially expand training data; rotation, crop, noise for images.
What is the active learning
Select most informative examples to label; reduce annotation cost.
Explain the semi-supervised learning
Leverage unlabeled data alongside labeled data.
What is the self-supervised learning
Create labels from data itself; contrastive learning.
Explain the unsupervised clustering
Group data points without labels; k-means, GMM, hierarchical.
What is the dimensionality reduction PCA
Project to principal components; maximize variance.
Explain the t-SNE visualization
Non-linear embedding for 2D visualization; respects local structure.
What is the manifold learning
Assume data lies on low-dimensional manifold.
Explain the kernel methods
Implicit mapping to high-dimensional space; kernel trick O(n^2).
What is the support vector machine SVM
Maximum margin classifier; convex optimization.
Explain the soft margin SVM
Allow misclassification; trade-off via slack variables.
What is the multiclass SVM
One-vs-rest or one-vs-one for multiple classes.
Explain the kernel trick optimization
Compute dot product in high-dim space implicitly.
What is the Gaussian process regression
Bayesian non-parametric; posterior over functions.
Explain the kernel selection
RBF, polynomial, linear kernels with different properties.
What is the decision tree splitting
Information gain or Gini impurity for node splitting.
Explain the random forest ensemble
Aggregate multiple trees on bootstrap samples.
What is the gradient boosting
Sequentially improve via residual fitting in function space.
Explain the AdaBoost algorithm
Weighted resampling focusing on hard examples.
What is the bagging vs boosting
Bagging parallel; boosting sequential; different error types.
Explain the mixture of experts
Gating network selects expert for input.
What is the expectation maximization EM
Alternately infer hidden variables and optimize likelihood.
Explain the variational inference
Approximate posterior with tractable distribution.
What is the Gibbs sampling
Iteratively sample from conditional distributions.
Explain the Markov chain Monte Carlo
Sample from target distribution via Markov chain.
What is the Metropolis-Hastings
Accept-reject sampling for MCMC.
Explain the Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
Use gradient information for efficient sampling.
What is the variational autoencoder
Autoencoder with latent variable KL divergence.
Explain the generative adversarial network
Generator and discriminator competition.
What is the Wasserstein GAN
Use Wasserstein distance for training stability.
Explain the style transfer
Combine content of one image with style of another.
What is the image segmentation
Pixel-level classification; semantic or instance segmentation.
Explain the object detection YOLO
Single-stage detector; predictions via grid cells.
What is the faster RCNN
Two-stage: region proposal then classification.
Explain the mask RCNN
Extend Faster RCNN with instance segmentation mask.
What is the feature pyramid network
Multi-scale features from hierarchical backbone.
Explain the attention visualization
Saliency maps or attention weights show what model uses.
What is the interpretability explainability
Understand model decisions; LIME, SHAP, attention.
Explain the adversarial examples
Imperceptible perturbations fool trained models.
What is the adversarial training
Train with adversarial examples for robustness.
Explain the certified robustness
Formal bounds on robustness via randomized smoothing.
What is the neural verification
Prove properties of networks via SMT solvers.
Explain the out-of-distribution detection
Identify inputs not from training distribution.
What is the uncertainty estimation
Model confidence in predictions via Bayesian or ensemble.
Explain the calibration confidence
Predicted probability matches actual frequency.
What is the Brier score
Mean squared error between prediction and outcome.
Explain the expected calibration error
Average difference between predicted and actual accuracy bins.
What is the confusion matrix metrics
Precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC for classification.
Explain the Precision vs Recall tradeoff
Precision: true positive rate; recall: coverage of positives.
What is the micro vs macro averaging
Micro: aggregate confusion matrices; macro: average per-class.
Explain the loss function choices
MSE regression; cross-entropy classification; domain-specific losses.
What is the Focal loss imbalance
Down-weight easy examples; focus on hard negatives.
Explain the Huber loss robustness
Quadratic near zero; linear in tails; robust outliers.
What is the triplet loss metric
Minimize distance to positive; maximize to negative.
Explain the contrastive learning
Learn representation by bringing similar examples close.
What is the supervised contrastive loss
Extend contrastive to labeled classes.
Explain the noise contrastive estimation
Approximate softmax by contrasting data vs noise.
What is the information bottleneck
Balance compression and prediction performance.
Explain the mutual information
Shared information between variables; measured in nats/bits.
What is the entropy lower bound
Variability limit in maximum likelihood estimation.
Explain the minimum description length
Model quality as compression; shorter descriptions better.
What is the Occam razor principle
Prefer simpler models; bias-variance tradeoff.
What is the bias-variance decomposition
Error = bias^2 + variance + noise. Models with high bias underfit; high variance overfit.
Explain the learning curve analysis
Plot training vs validation error vs data size; identify underfitting/overfitting.
What is the statistical significance testing
Hypothesis test model improvement; t-test, permutation test for validity.
Explain the effect size interpretation
Magnitude of effect beyond statistical significance.
What is the multiple hypothesis correction
Bonferroni or FDR to control false positives in multiple tests.
Explain the P-value misinterpretation
P-value is probability of data given null; not probability null is false.
What is the confidence interval
Range likely containing true parameter with specified confidence.
Explain the Bayesian posterior
Update beliefs with data via Bayes rule; express uncertainty.
What is the prior selection
Choose prior based on domain knowledge or use uninformative.
Explain the conjugate prior
Prior and likelihood from same family; closed-form posterior.
What is the Monte Carlo approximation
Approximate integral via random sampling.
Explain the importance sampling
Sample from proposal; reweight by likelihood ratio for target.
What is the rejection sampling
Accept/reject based on comparison to reference; inefficient high-dim.
Explain the Langevin dynamics
Add noise to gradient descent; converges to target distribution.
What is the score matching
Match gradient of log density without computing partition function.
Explain the denoising score matching
Perturb data with noise; score matches derivative.
What is the diffusion model
Reverse process of adding noise; generative via denoising.
Explain the flow-based model
Invertible transformation to simple distribution.
What is the normalizing flow
Stack bijections with tractable Jacobians; compute likelihoods.
Explain the autoregressive model
Decompose joint as product of conditionals; sample sequentially.
What is the causal inference
Estimate treatment effect; confounding and selection bias challenges.
Explain the propensity score
Probability of treatment given covariates; match treated-control.
What is the instrumental variable
Variable affecting treatment but not outcome directly.
Explain the difference-in-differences
Control for time trends via unaffected group comparison.
What is the regression discontinuity
Exploit threshold in assignment for causal identification.
Explain the randomized controlled trial
Gold standard: random assignment eliminates confounding.
What is the A/B testing framework
Compare two variants; power analysis determines sample size.
Explain the sequential analysis
Monitor results during experiment; early stopping rules.
What is the multiple testing correction
Adjust significance threshold for multiple comparisons.
Explain the clinical trial phases
Phase 1: safety; Phase 2: efficacy; Phase 3: confirmation.
What is the intention-to-treat
Analyze per assignment; respect randomization.
Explain the per-protocol analysis
Analyze per actual treatment; can introduce bias.
What is the treatment effect heterogeneity
Effect varies by subgroup; estimate conditional effects.
Explain the causal forest
Random forest variant estimating heterogeneous treatment effects.
What is the orthogonal machine learning
Debiased ML for treatment effect estimation with high-dim.
Explain the double machine learning
Double robust: estimate via two ML models for robustness.
What is the surrogacy
Use intermediate outcome predicting final outcome.
Explain the mediation analysis
Decompose total effect into direct and indirect.
What is the path analysis
Model causal paths using regression coefficients.
Explain the structural equation model
Latent variables and causal paths; SEM estimation.
What is the factor analysis
Extract latent factors from observed variables.
Explain the dimensionality reduction factor
Reduce noise via latent factor representation.
What is the exploratory factor analysis
Data-driven latent structure discovery.
Explain the confirmatory factor analysis
Test predefined latent structure.
What is the principal component analysis PCA
Maximize variance in projection direction.
Explain the whitening preprocessing
Decorrelate variables and normalize variance.
What is the independent component analysis
Recover independent sources from mixed observations.
Explain the non-negative matrix factorization
Factorize into non-negative factors; interpretable.
What is the tensor decomposition
Extend matrix factorization to higher orders.
Explain the Tucker decomposition
Core tensor times factor matrices.
What is the CP decomposition
Sum of rank-1 tensors; interpretable factors.
Explain the graph neural network
Message passing on graphs; aggregate neighbor features.
What is the graph embedding
Learn low-dim representation of nodes; DeepWalk, Node2Vec.
Explain the node classification
Predict node label given neighborhood and features.
What is the link prediction
Predict missing or future edges; similarity or latent features.
Explain the graph classification
Assign class to entire graph; pooling and graph-level features.
What is the knowledge graph embedding
Learn embeddings for entities and relations.
Explain the triple classification
Predict if (subject, relation, object) is true.
What is the relation extraction
Identify relations between entities in text.
Explain the entity linking
Map named entities to knowledge base entries.
What is the coreference resolution
Identify which mentions refer to same entity.
Explain the dependency parsing
Extract grammatical dependencies between words.
What is the semantic role labeling
Identify predicate-argument structure in sentence.
Explain the constituency parsing
